{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / The Associated Press)

**Document:** Exhibit 10.14 — Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February
**Our party:** The Associated Press ("AP" / Customer)
**Counterparty:** Kubient (Vendor)
**Prepared by:** In-house counsel

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us: it is expressly non-exclusive (Section 1), carries no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment, no liquidated damages and no audit right running against us, and Kubient gives real, continuing performance warranties (Section 9(b)) that are not swallowed by the Section 13 disclaimer. Assignment (Section (h)) and governing law/venue (Section 14(a) — Delaware law, New York courts) are acceptable, the latter sitting at the playbook fallback.

Four gaps require action. First and most serious, there is **no monetary limitation of liability anywhere in the document** — Section 7 waives consequential damages only, leaving our direct liability uncapped. Second, the Section 2 platform licence is **"revocable"** without qualification and runs to "Customer" alone, so Kubient can in principle pull it at will and our Affiliates and contractors are excluded. Third, the Agreement has **no IP/ownership article**, so ownership of AP Content, Requests and visitor data is unallocated even though Kubient collects and stores that data. Fourth, Section 4(c) permits Kubient to **"return or destroy"** our Confidential Information at its own election, with no transition assistance and no data-return right. We also propose shortening the 90-day post-Initial-Term notice to 30 days (60 as fallback) and inserting a standard vendor insurance covenant.

Four findings did not clear internal verification and are marked **needs review** below; they should be confirmed by the reviewer before we transmit any position on them.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section (as recorded) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 7) | No monetary cap anywhere; fails fallback (12 months' fees). Redline: mutual greater-of cap using amounts paid or payable between the Parties with a USD 1,000,000 floor, standard uncapped carve-outs, and confirmation that revenue-share amounts owed are not "damages". Mutual consequential-damages waiver left intact. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 2; Section 6(a)) | Grant is expressly "revocable" without qualifier and covers "Customer" only; Section 6(a) bars third-party access absent Kubient's prior written approval. Redline: extend to AP Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (not "prohibited third-party access"; AP responsible for compliance) and limit revocation to expiration or termination under Section 4. |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Preamble | No ownership article. Redline: new General Provisions (j) — AP retains rights in its Content, Properties and data; Kubient keeps its platform and pre-existing tools; deliverables created for AP assigned to AP with perpetual royalty-free licence to embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 4(a)) | Assessed as compliant at the fallback: either Party may terminate for any reason after the one-year Initial Term on 90 days' notice, within the 60–90 day window, symmetric, no multi-year lock-in. No redline proposed. Verification did not clear — confirm before relying. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section (h)) | Mutual restriction with affiliate/asset-purchaser/merger-successor carve-out and consent not unreasonably withheld; no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right for Kubient. No bar on assignment to an AP competitor — noted only. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 1) | Non-exclusivity expressly confirmed; AP free to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant on AP; only ordinary platform-use and confidentiality obligations. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble (clause reviewed: Sections 4(a), 5) | No penalty, shortfall or minimum-fee obligation on AP; Section 4(a) fees "generated during the termination period" flow from Kubient to AP under the revenue share. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 4(a)) | Successive 1-year renewals are acceptable, but the only post-Initial-Term exit is 90 days' notice, exceeding the 60-day fallback ceiling. Redline: 30 days, exercisable as a non-renewal election; 60 days offered as fallback. No unilateral uplift mechanic, so the CPI/3% cap is not engaged. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 4(c)) | Each Party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its election; no transition assistance, no usable-format data return, no deletion certification. Redline: new 4(c)(v) — up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification, overriding the destroy option for Customer Data; 90-day fallback flagged in comment. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Needs review** | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 5) | Assessed as compliant: Kubient has no audit, records or inspection right against us, so nothing to constrain. No redline. Verification did not clear — confirm before relying. Separately parked: Impressions are measured solely as measured by Kubient, with no AP-side verification right. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review** | Preamble | Assessed as compliant at the preferred position: no non-solicit, no-hire or recruitment covenant on AP; the independent contractor clause creates no implied covenant and the survival list omits any such term. No redline (flagging would invite Kubient to add one). Verification did not clear — confirm before relying. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 14(a)) | Delaware law (playbook fallback) with exclusive jurisdiction in New York, New York state and federal courts (preferred venue). Noted only: Section 8 provides for AAA Commercial Rules arbitration, which sits awkwardly with the exclusive-court wording; AAA-administered and domestic, so no walk-away. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN or price-matching mechanic; Section 1 preserves our freedom to use other agents or third parties. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (clause reviewed: Sections 1, 5) | Pure revenue share on actual revenue; no committed spend, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap. Kubient guarantees no minimum revenue level; the Winning Bid Price floor is set by AP and benefits us. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Preamble (clause reviewed: Sections 9(b), 13) | Continuing warranties "now and throughout the Term" (material conformance to industry standards, freedom from utility-affecting errors, no malicious code, compliance with Laws, non-infringement/ownership); at least 12 months given the 1-year auto-renewing Term. Section 13 disclaimer is confined to implied warranties. No express repair/replace/refund remedy — noted only; pressing it risks a narrower Vendor-elected exclusive remedy. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Needs review** | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 10) | Genuine Vendor indemnity with defence, fees and standard procedure, but no express third-party IP-infringement limb (reached only derivatively via the breach-of-warranty limb and the non-infringement warranty). Proposed minimal edit: new limb (vi) covering any allegation or claim that the Services, Auction Platform or deliverables infringe third-party IP. Verification did not clear — confirm before transmitting. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Preamble (clause reviewed: Section 14) | No insurance or certificate requirement, although Kubient hosts the platform and collects, maintains and stores visitor data. Redline: new Section 14(j) — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in comment. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following reach, or sit at the edge of, walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **No liability cap (LOL-CAP, Section 7).** The absence of any monetary cap fails the fallback on a material term and leaves our direct liability unlimited. A "fees paid by Customer" cap would be illusory here because, under Section 5, payment flows from Kubient to AP — hence the greater-of formulation with a USD 1,000,000 floor.
2. **Licence revocable at will (LICENSE, Section 2).** An unqualified "revocable" grant means Kubient may withdraw platform access during the Term rather than only on expiration or uncured material breach. Revocation must be tied to expiration or termination under Section 4.
3. **Election to destroy our data on termination (TRANSITION, Section 4(c)).** Kubient may elect destruction, with no return right and no transition assistance — at or near the walk-away position of no data return / immediate deletion, and short of even the 90-day fallback.
4. **No insurance for a vendor processing our data (INSURANCE).** Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, on its own warranty, collects, maintains and stores visitor data; no coverage requirement is the walk-away scenario for a data-processing vendor.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the four needs-review findings** (T4C, AUDIT, NOSOLICIT, INDEMN) before anything is sent. Three are assessed as compliant with no redline; only INDEMN carries a proposed edit. We should not transmit a position on any of them until verification is cleared.
2. **Issue the redline package** in priority order: (i) mutual liability cap with uncapped carve-outs in Section 7; (ii) licence scope and revocability in Section 2 (with the Section 6(a) conforming point); (iii) new ownership clause as General Provisions (j); (iv) new Section 4(c)(v) transition assistance and data return; (v) 90 to 30 days' notice in Section 4(a), with 60 days as our stated fallback; (vi) new Section 14(j) insurance covenant, with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback flagged; and, if confirmed, (vii) the express IP limb (vi) in Section 10.
3. **Obtain and review the Exhibits.** Fee terms, revenue-share percentages and any committed volumes sit in Exhibits not included in the reviewed document. If an Exhibit introduces an early-termination or shortfall payment by AP, it should be capped at three months' fees per the fallback; committed volumes or spend would reopen MINCOMMIT.
4. **Raise revenue verification.** Impressions are measured solely as measured by Kubient and the revenue share runs through the Exhibits with no AP-side verification right. This runs in our favour to fix and should be added to the negotiation list.
5. **Housekeeping if drafting reopens.** Align Section 8 (AAA arbitration) with the exclusive court forum in Section 14(a); consider a bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor. Neither is worth a standalone exchange.
6. **Negotiation file note (no action now).** If Kubient later proposes a non-solicit, our ceiling is a mutual covenant limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire."}
